title: Unified hosted multimode endpoint PRD: progressive rollouts, tiering, and launch checklist
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary: This PRD defines a single hosted inference surface that consolidates chat, completion, embedding, and rerank behaviors behind a unified endpoint and a tiered routing layer. Goal: reduce fragmentation of hosted endpoints, simplify SDK surface, enable progressive rollouts by tenant/region, and provide clear behavioral and SLO guarantees for each lane.

Background: Redwood currently exposes multiple overlapping hosted endpoints that differ by protocol, model variants, and fallback behavior. Customers building multi-feature flows (e.g., search+rerank+chat) repeatedly configure multiple endpoints, increasing integration complexity and surface area for regressions. Consolidating to a multimode hosted surface reduces cognitive load, enables centralized telemetry and tiered routing (by latency/cost/accuracy), and gives us one rollout path for quality gates.

Scope (in): Unified REST surface for modes: chat, completion, embedding, rerank; request-level mode field; routing policy configuration by account tier (free/standard/enterprise); model-variant mapping table; streaming for chat/completion; structured output contract for rerank responses; SDK adapters for JS/Python.

Scope (out): New model training, on-device SDKs, delegated third-party models, and on-prem private deployments (covered by separate Private workstreams).

Non-goals: merging internal legacy endpoints at the infra level in first rollout — we will route legacy traffic to the adapter proxy for migration.
acceptance_criteria: Unified endpoint accepts a 'mode' parameter with allowed values: chat, completion, embedding, rerank and validates mode-specific schema at the API gateway.
Behavioral contracts published: chat conversation state handling, completion stop/tokenization behavior, embedding vector shape and normalization, rerank scoring range and explanation field.
Streaming output supported for chat and completion with identical chunking and tokenization semantics as existing hosted streaming behavior.
Tiered routing honors account tiers and resolves to correct model variants; routing table configurable via Console and feature-flagged for rollout.
Per-route telemetry emitted: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens per request, cost estimate, model fallback reason; dashboards pre-populated in Datadog/Grafana.
SLOs defined and met in staging for first 30 days: chat median latency < 250ms per token at 95th percentile for small models; system gracefully degrades to region fallback under capacity events.
SDKs (JS and Python) include adapters with backward-compatible client calls for chat/completion/embeddings/rerank and integration tests that exercise all modes.
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for request metadata and audit logging in dedicated and hosted modes.
Migration playbook documented and verified via a canary run with 5 internal customers with monitoring and rollback hooks.
Launch checklist items in this ticket marked done and cross-linked PRs merged: API gateway changes, runtime kernel mappings, console routing UI, telemetry dashboards, SDK release tags.
launch_checklist: API gateway schema change deployed behind feature flag
Runtime changes: kernel mapping and quantization profiles validated in staging
Routing table prototype populated and Console UI for override in place
SDK adapters released (js v1.9.0, python v0.22.0) and smoke-tested
End-to-end canary: 5 internal tenants onboarded to feature-flagged endpoint
Datadog dashboards and alerts (latency, error rate, fallback rate) provisioned
Security review completed and audit logging validated
Documentation: PRD published, public API spec updated, migration guide posted to Confluence
Runbook: incident playbook, rollback steps, and revert flags documented
Go/No-Go review scheduled with Eng, Product, Design, Security, and SRE attendees
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-11: Use single 'mode' field rather than multiple endpoints to simplify SDK ergonomics (Priya, Marco, Leah)
Trade-off: Early-unification increases risk of cross-mode regressions; mitigations include strict schema validation and per-mode integration tests
Will not hard-deprecate legacy endpoints at launch; instead use adapter proxy to give teams 90-day migration window
Routing policy: initial tiers=free/standard/enterprise; enterprise gets priority routing and deterministic fallbacks
Model variants: small/medium/large families will be exposed with explicit latency and cost tags in the model catalog
stakeholder_approvals: SRE: Aisha Malik - approved pending telemetry knobs 2025-02-14
migration_plan_high_level: Phase 0: Internal canary - route 2% of internal traffic via feature flag to exercise cabinets and KV cache behavior
Phase 1: Early customers - enroll 5 beta customers and collect qualitative feedback and eval regressions
Phase 2: Gradual rollout - by account tier and region, increase traffic to unified endpoint over 4 weeks
Phase 3: Cutover window - once telemetry shows stability, deprecate legacy SDK warnings and provide migration automation
Phase 4: Post-launch audit - 30/60/90 day quality reviews, model-level regression checks tied to eval prompt sets
telemetry_and_slo: Emit per-request attributes: mode, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, route_decision, fallback_reason
Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency by mode and region, token throughput, fallback rate, cost per 1k tokens by variant
Alerts: fallback_rate > 3% sustained for 5m; error_rate > 0.5% p95; sustained p95 latency > target across three regions
SLO targets defined for launch and first-quarter review
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag at gateway level to route all traffic to legacy adapter
Revert model routing table to previous stable snapshot
Trigger incident runbook and notify customers in the beta cohort
Postmortem and targeted fixes before reattempting rollout
